title: Atomistic Modeling of Chemical Disorder in Materials: Bridging Conventional Methods and AI-Assisted Approaches
abstract: arXiv:2605.19124v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Chemical disorder, originating from the mixed occupation of crystallographic sites by multiple elements, is widespread in alloys, ceramics, and compositionally complex materials, where short- and long-range orderings strongly influence properties. A central obstacle is the representation gap between experiments and simulations: experiments often report disorder as partial occupancies and ensemble-averaged behaviors, whereas atomistic simulations and AI workflows usually require fully specified configurations. Tackling this gap requires computational methods that convert averaged disorder descriptions into representative configurational ensembles while balancing cost, bias, and fidelity. This challenge has become more urgent in AI-driven computational discovery, where ignoring disorder may cause AI workflows to misrank stability, misjudge novelty, and misdirect experiments with too-idealized representations. translated_title: 材料中化学无序的原子尺度建模：连接传统方法与AI辅助方法
translated_abstract: 化学无序源于多种元素对晶体学位点的混合占位，广泛存在于合金、陶瓷和成分复杂材料中，其中短程和长程有序强烈影响材料性能。一个核心障碍是实验与模拟之间的表示鸿沟：实验通常以部分占位率和系综平均行为来描述无序，而原子尺度模拟和AI工作流通常需要完全指定的构型。解决这一鸿沟需要能够将平均化无序描述转换为代表性构型系综的计算方法，同时兼顾成本、偏差和保真度。在AI驱动的计算发现中，这一挑战变得更为紧迫，因为忽略无序可能导致AI工作流错误排序稳定性、误判新颖性，并以过于理想化的表示误导实验方向。本综述重点（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本综述系统梳理了材料中化学无序的原子尺度建模方法，核心在于弥合实验中平均化无序描述与模拟及AI工作流所需的完全指定构型之间的表示鸿沟。
en_tdlr: This review surveys atomistic modeling methods for chemical disorder in materials, focusing on bridging the representation gap between ensemble-averaged experimental descriptions and the fully specified configurations required by simulations and AI-assisted workflows.
